record.paper_title: The Quest for Equational Axiomatizations of Parallel Composition: Status and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Observation congruence over a CCS fragment
record.original_question: Prove that observation congruence is not finitely equationally axiomatizable over the fragment of CCS that excludes recursion, relabelling, and restriction.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the fragment of Milner's Calculus of Communicating Systems (CCS) generated by the grammar
  P ::= 0 | x | a.P | τ.P | P + P | P | P,
where a ranges over a fixed countable set of visible (observable) actions A, τ is the distinguished silent (internal) action, x ranges over a countable set of process variables, "0" is the inactive process, "a.P" and "τ.P" are action prefixing, "+" is nondeterministic choice, and "|" is the parallel composition operator (allowing communication between matching co-actions a and ā). The fragment explicitly excludes recursion, the relabelling operator, and the restriction operator.

The operational semantics is the standard one for CCS, generating a labelled transition system whose labels are A ∪ {ā : a ∈ A} ∪ {τ}. Weak bisimilarity ≈ is defined as the largest symmetric relation R such that whenever P R Q and P →^a P', there exists Q' with Q ⇒^a Q' and P' R Q', where ⇒^a denotes the weak transition relation (sequences of τ-transitions surrounding the action a, with τ-transitions absorbed when a = τ). Observation congruence ≈^c is the largest congruence (with respect to all operators of the fragment) that is included in weak bisimilarity; equivalently, P ≈^c Q iff for every action μ, P →^μ P' implies Q ⇒^μ Q' with P' ≈ Q', and symmetrically.

A finite equational axiomatization of ≈^c over this fragment is a finite set E of equations between open terms of the fragment such that for all closed terms P, Q of the fragment, E ⊢ P = Q (using the standard rules of equational logic) iff P ≈^c Q.

Problem: Prove that no such finite equational axiomatization exists; equivalently, show that observation congruence is not finitely equationally axiomatizable over the recursion-, relabelling-, and restriction-free fragment of CCS.
artifact.status_search_result: Surveys and follow-up work on equational axiomatizations of CCS-style parallel composition explicitly list the non-finite-axiomatizability of observation (weak) congruence over the recursion-, relabelling-, and restriction-free fragment of CCS as an open problem, with the negative answer only conjectured. Related results have been obtained for strong bisimilarity (Moller's negative result) and for branching bisimilarity, and finite bases exist when auxiliary operators (left merge, communication merge) are added, but no resolution of the observation-congruence case over the pure CCS fragment has been found in the literature through 2026.

status_evidence.title: The Quest for Equational Axiomatizations of Parallel Composition: Status and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: no finite equational axiomatization ... over the recursion, relabelling and restriction free version of CCS
status_evidence.claim: The non-finite-axiomatizability of observation congruence over this CCS fragment is listed as an open problem, with the negative answer conjectured.

status_evidence.title: CCS with Hennessy's Merge has no Finite Equational Axiomatization (BRICS RS-03-34)
status_evidence.snippet: the recursion free fragment of Milner's Calculus of Communicating Systems ... is not finitely based modulo bisimulation equivalence
status_evidence.claim: Negative results are known for related variants (Hennessy's merge, strong bisimilarity), but not for observation congruence over pure CCS without restriction/relabelling.

status_evidence.title: On the Axiomatisation of Branching Bisimulation Congruence over CCS
status_evidence.snippet: CCS is not finitely based modulo rooted branching bisimilarity
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2022) work resolves the branching bisimilarity case but does not address observation (weak) congruence over the restriction- and relabelling-free fragment.
